reason: The passage explicitly depicts Yahweh's active antagonism toward the Hebrew people. It states 'כִּי עַל־אַף יְהוָה הָיְתָה בִירוּשָׁלִם וּבִיהוּדָה' ('For the anger of Yahweh was upon Jerusalem and upon Judah'), describing His wrath being directed at them. The text then details Yahweh's antagonistic actions: allowing the siege of Jerusalem, the destruction of the Temple ('וַיִּשְׂרֹף אֶת־בֵּית־יְהוָה'), the breaking of city walls, and the exile of the people. The passage characterizes these as divinely-sanctioned military conquests that result in the displacement of the Hebrew people from their land. While the antagonism is presented as a response to the people's wickedness ('וַיַּעַשׂ הָרַע בְּעֵינֵי יְהוָה'), the passage unambiguously portrays Yahweh as acting in direct opposition to the Hebrew people's continued existence in their homeland.
